feature: Canonical Prisma relational model for tenant, operations, guest/auth, financial, push, outbound and presence domains
semantic_review_notes: All 84 models were re-read in bounded ranges and inventoried by model/range/relation/unique/index shape after QA challenge. Tenant/config group Organization/Location/operating-hours/Guest information (501-775) uses organization-scoped Location keys and Restrict relations; GuestLocationPrivacy points to immutable versioned GuestPrivacyPublication while the active pointer is nullable. Auth group User/StaffAuthSession/UserMfaTotpFactor/MfaRecoveryCode/StaffRefreshCredential (777-872) separates access-token, refresh-token, protected TOTP and recovery verifier material; session-to-factor is scoped by [userId,mfaFactorId], refresh replacement is scoped by [sessionId,id], token hashes/selectors and generation slots are unique. Staff/operational group OrganizationMembership through HandoffVerification (874-1707) repeatedly exposes composite tenant/location/session identity: ValetSession binds Location/Vehicle/Customer/ParkingZone/ParkingSpot/KeySlot and membership actors through organization/location keys, Task and DispatchEvent use organization+location+session+task scope, tracking/GPS/geofence chains preserve that scope, and condition-photo operation/attempt/verification models use unusually wide composite keys to bind actor/session/object identity across retry and verification records. GuestBrowserEnrollment/GuestBrowserSession (1196-1235) make enrollment/browser token hashes unique and browser session generation unique; GuestPushRegistration later binds [guestBrowserSessionId,valetSessionId,credentialGeneration]. Financial group Payment/PaymentCollectionOperation/Validation/CashEntry/PaymentProviderEvent/Refund (1709-1858) uses organization-scoped payment FKs plus tenant idempotency/provider-reference uniqueness and validation supersession scoped to the same payment. Push/outbound group (1926-2333) preserves intent/delivery registration identity and retry/lease indexes; Stage C outbound separates recipientDigest from the encrypted OutboundMessageEnvelope and snapshots permission/policy/binding revisions in OutboundMessageIntent. Audit/security group AuditEvent/AccountSecurityAuditEvent/AntiAbuseEvent (2335-2392) keeps tenant actor relations where applicable and pagination/retention indexes. Shift Presence group (2521-2694) uses organization/location/member/user/action scoped operation/challenge/decision/exception keys and immutable management-result/audit linkage. Atypical relation-light tables such as OutboundMessagingControl and AntiAbuseEvent intentionally have no relational FK surface. The schema itself explicitly delegates Stage C outbound CHECK/partial indexes/security functions (line 2100), anti-abuse partial group/window index (2389), and DEC-099 extra Shift/zone/decision/reviewer FKs plus lifecycle guards (2662-2663) to SQL migrations; those constraints must not be inferred from Prisma alone.
callers_consumers: Database migrations and API SQL code target the mapped tables/enums/relations
invariants_error_checks: Model inventory found 84 models. Owning relations overwhelmingly specify onDelete:Restrict; scoped operational/financial relations use composite organization/location/session/payment keys where the parent exposes matching unique keys. Representative hard fences include OrganizationMembership [organizationId,id,userId], ValetSession [organizationId,locationId,id], Task [organizationId,locationId,valetSessionId,id], GuestBrowserSession [id,valetSessionId,credentialGeneration], Payment [organizationId,id], Refund [organizationId,paymentId,id], and the wide condition-photo verification keys. Auth tokens/selectors/idempotency/provider references carry unique constraints. Exceptions are documented relation-light control/event tables and SQL-migration-owned CHECK/partial/lifecycle invariants, so schema review does not treat absent Prisma checks as absent database protection.
test_refs: Historical references only; no tests rerun in C003
limits: Prisma cannot express several SQL-owned guards/partial indexes documented at lines 2100, 2389, and 2662-2663; migration bodies remain the authority for those invariants

feature: Management MFA TOTP step-up with replay and authority rechecks
semantic_review_notes: Step-up resolves the current bearer session, reserves a user-scoped TOTP anti-abuse slot, then performs all security checks in one PostgreSQL transaction: re-lock/recheck the auth session, lock the user, re-evaluate management-MFA eligibility, lock the current factor, require ACTIVE state, decrypt the factor secret with user+factor binding, verify the code strictly after any prior accepted time step, update last_accepted_step only while the factor is still ACTIVE, and establish assurance on the same session/factor at the same database operation time. This ordering fences concurrent logout/refresh replay/factor replacement and serializes TOTP replay. Verification failures are counted by anti-abuse; infrastructure/security-unavailable failures do not consume the bad-code budget.

feature: Staff invitation activation with anti-enumeration password verification and dual anti-abuse bounds
semantic_review_notes: Activation first derives a trusted client address and reserves a 30-attempt address budget, then a tighter five-attempt invite-token credential budget. It hashes the invite token before database lookup. A genuinely pending account with no password may set a newly policy-validated Argon2 password; every other path performs an Argon2 verification against either the accepted stored hash or a fixed dummy hash, avoiding a fast invalid-token/unsupported-hash oracle. Only an already ACTIVE account with a supported matching password may converge to ALREADY_ACTIVATED; all other cases use the same StaffActivationFailedError. The authoritative DB activation and successful reservation finalization occur in one transaction. Failed credentials count anti-abuse reservations, while successful/idempotent activation reservations are ignored rather than consuming failure budgets.
invariants_error_checks: Unavailable trusted client address fails as AntiAbuseUnavailable. Invalid password policy on first activation cannot reach password hashing. Token lookup uses only the hash. Dummy Argon2 verification preserves work for invalid/unsupported states. DB race outcome is authoritative in the final transaction.

feature: Browser staff login, refresh-cookie rotation and logout transport
semantic_review_notes: The browser auth surface requires an explicitly allowed Origin on login, refresh and logout, requires JSON and rejects query/body authority outside the strict contracts. Login returns only access credentials in the response body, exposes the logical staff session UUID separately as continuity metadata, and stores the refresh token only in a Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /v1/staff/auth with no Domain attribute. Refresh requires an empty body and exactly one refresh cookie name; malformed/missing/duplicate cookie authority is treated as generic authentication failure and clears the browser cookie. A successful refresh rotates the server refresh credential and replaces the cookie with the remaining absolute-session lifetime. Transport/Origin failures occur before credential consumption and therefore do not clear or rotate a valid credential. Logout is intentionally idempotent/non-disclosing, delegates server revocation by refresh credential when present, then clears the cookie.
invariants_error_checks: Cookie attributes are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/v1/staff/auth and host-scoped. readRefreshCookie rejects duplicate cookie names before parsing. Refresh/logout accept no user/session/tenant identifier from the client. StaffAuthOriginPolicy is checked before the auth service. Web response contract excludes refreshToken and staffAuthSessionId from the body.

feature: Staff password authentication, opaque session issuance and refresh-family rotation/replay revocation
semantic_review_notes: Login performs one Argon2 verification for every account state, using a fixed accepted dummy hash for unknown/passwordless/unsupported stored hashes and the real accepted hash otherwise. Only ACTIVE users with a supported matching password proceed. Before session issuance the transaction takes the per-user security advisory lock and rechecks the exact password hash plus ACTIVE status, fencing concurrent password/status changes. Access and refresh credentials are independent 256-bit random tokens; only domain-separated SHA-256 hashes are persisted. Session/access lifetime is 15 minutes bounded by a fixed 720-hour absolute session expiry, and the refresh expires at the same absolute boundary. Successful login finalizes any identifier anti-abuse reservation inside the same transaction so session creation cannot commit while limiter finalization fails. Refresh validates syntax, hashes the credential, obtains the same user security boundary, then locks refresh/session/user rows. A consumed refresh is treated as replay and atomically revokes the whole session family. Expired/revoked/disabled-user refresh likewise revokes the session. A valid refresh consumes the old credential, creates exactly one next-generation credential expiring at the unchanged absolute session deadline, links replaced_by_credential_id, rotates the access hash and clamps access/cookie lifetime to the absolute expiry. The old access token becomes stale because current_access_token_hash changes. Concurrent same-token refreshes therefore produce one winner and one replay revocation, intentionally invalidating the family after detected reuse.
callers_consumers: DatabaseStaffPrincipal/SessionContext resolvers consume current access-token hash and session expiry
invariants_error_checks: Generic StaffAuthenticationError covers unknown account, malformed/invalid/expired/replayed refresh and disabled/revoked state. Login transaction rechecks state/hash after expensive verification. Refresh uses database clock, FOR UPDATE on credential/session/user after the per-user advisory lock, preserves absolute expiry and revokes on replay. One-current-refresh-per-session and expiry constraints are database-backed. Raw tokens are never persisted.
